newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Unit of Windhorst group says settles HK claim.
newsitem.headline: Unit of Windhorst group says settles HK claim.

text.p: Windhorst Far East Services Ltd, a unit of the diversified trading group founded by young German entrepreneur Lars Windhorst, said on Monday it had settled a civil claim with a former director.

After an acrimonious split, Horst Vetter, a former director of Windhorst Far East Holdings, won a judgement against the company from Hong Kong's Labour Tribunal in December for HK$126,000 (US$16,300) in back pay, balance of annual leave pay and costs.

Friedrich Langer, director of Windhorst Asia Pacific Holdings unit Windhorst Land Development Ltd, told Reuters the firm had issued a cheque to Vetter for the full amount of the judgement, which had been deposited with the Labour Tribunal.
"We had a dispute and Mr Windhorst signed his cheques on the 6th of January in Germany and I just brought them over from Germany," Langer said.
The delay in payment was due to the Christmas holidays and the need to consult lawyers in Germany, Langer said.

On Monday, Vetter accompanied a District Court bailiff into the offices of Windhorst Asia Pacific Holdings in the luxury Central Plaza skyscraper on Hong Kong island after the 14-day payment period elapsed.
"The amount in question, including fees, is approximately HK$130,000," Vetter said, adding that the value of the items to be seized and sold would likely not cover the judgement.
Vetter halted the bailiff's inventory after speaking with Langer, but said later that a check with the Labour Tribunal showed that no cheque had been deposited in his name.
"There is no proof any money has been paid in yet," he told Reuters.
Vetter added that he would wait a few days before deciding on his next course of action.

Windhorst, the 20-year-old chairman of Windhorst Asia Pacific Holdings Ltd, became the darling of the German press after he founded a computer firm at 16 and expanded into a diversified trading empire.
German Chancellor Helmut Kohl called Windhorst "an example to us all" and took him on a trade mission to Vietnam in November 1995.
Last July, prosecutors in Bielefeld, Germany, ended a probe into Windhorst's empire after Vetter accused him of misappropriating funds and misrepresenting the wealth of his company in a brochure.
The prosecutors said they had no grounds for filing charges. ($1 = HK$7.73)
